abstract: Maintains non-destructive tomography certifications and electron microscopy preparation throughput records
system_message:
You are Materials Forensics Lead (MFL). The Materials Forensics Lead (MFL) maintains non-destructive tomography certifications, electron microscopy preparation throughput records, and microindentation hardness profiling data for candidate forensic investigation protocols.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Microindentation hardness profiling（HARD）
information_points.content:
MFL-HARD-ECT：According to metallurgical testing of extracted foreign particulate contact surfaces, the Confocal Raman and Micro-Tomographic Protocol indicates a substrate Vickers hardness of 180 HV under a 50 gram-force load.
MFL-HARD-YPY：According to metallurgical testing of extracted foreign particulate contact surfaces, the Focused Ion Beam Milling and Elemental Mapping Protocol indicates a substrate Vickers hardness of 210 HV under a 50 gram-force load.
MFL-HARD-FLB：According to metallurgical testing of extracted foreign particulate contact surfaces, the Synchrotron Micro-X-ray Fluorescence Protocol indicates a substrate Vickers hardness of 240 HV under a 50 gram-force load.

information_points.title: Maintains non-destructive tomography certifications and electron microscopy preparation throughput records（MATR）
information_points.content:
MFL-MATR-XXJ：For the Confocal Raman and Micro-Tomographic Protocol, non-destructive X-ray microtomography is certified for the candidate sub-micron volumetric imaging bench, and the transmission electron microscopy sample preparation throughput is 6 sample/day.
MFL-MATR-U8H：For the Synchrotron Micro-X-ray Fluorescence Protocol, non-destructive X-ray microtomography is not certified for the candidate sub-micron volumetric imaging bench, while the transmission electron microscopy sample preparation throughput is 6 sample/day.
MFL-MATR-RZT：For the Focused Ion Beam Milling and Elemental Mapping Protocol, non-destructive X-ray microtomography is certified for the candidate sub-micron volumetric imaging bench, and the transmission electron microscopy sample preparation throughput is 6 sample/day.
